title: Drona: Abhimanyu, Ghatotkacha, Drona's death
hook: the whole day becomes a race against the sun, and the sun seems to set too early

segments.voice: Yesterday Abhimanyu fell inside the wheel, and Arjuna made his vow: Jayadratha before sunset, or the fire. Your line: Drona: Abhimanyu, Ghatotkacha, Drona's death. Today, the sun is the clock. Day eight hundred thirty-four.

The news of Arjuna's vow reaches Jayadratha in the night, and he wants to leave the war and go home. Drona talks him out of it. Stay, he says, and I'll protect you. So in the morning Drona builds his army into layer after layer, and places Jayadratha far at the back, behind all of it. Arjuna has one day to cut through to a man hidden behind a whole army. Every hour the sun climbs, then starts to fall. Today, how that race ends.
screen: `JAYADRATHA WANTS TO FLEE.` → `DRONA HIDES HIM AT THE BACK.` → `ONE DAY, ONE SUN.`

segments.voice: Arjuna and Krishna drive into the ranks, and the fighting goes on hour after hour. At one point the horses are worn out. In Ganguli's telling, Arjuna stands guard with his bow while Krishna unyokes them, lets them drink and rest, right there in the middle of the battle, then harnesses them again. It's a strangely tender pause in a day of slaughter. But the sun keeps falling, and Jayadratha is still out of reach. Then the light fails. Darkness spreads over the field, and the text says Krishna brought it about by his own power. The Kaurava side sees what looks like sunset. They cheer. Arjuna has failed his vow. Jayadratha, safe at last, raises his head to look at the sky. Now, Krishna says. The sun is still up. And Arjuna's arrow takes Jayadratha's head. Krishna adds one warning. Jayadratha's father had once declared that whoever made his son's head fall to the ground would have his own head burst. So Arjuna's arrows carry the head away, and it falls into the father's lap as he sits at his evening worship. When the old king rises, startled, the head drops to the earth, and the curse falls on him instead. The epic tells it plainly: Krishna's darkness, a hidden man, a curse turned back on its maker. Some readers find the day troubling. Others see Krishna keeping a vow alive on a field where the rules had already broken around Abhimanyu. And Drona's turn is coming.
screen: `A REST FOR THE HORSES` · `DARKNESS BEFORE SUNSET` · `JAYADRATHA LOOKS UP` · then, large: `THE CURSE TURNS BACK`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let your shoulders drop. Think of something you're racing against today, a deadline, a promise, a clock. Breathe in, and feel how tight that race holds you. Breathe out, and give yourself a pause, the way Krishna gave the horses water in the middle of the fight. The race will still be there in two minutes. For now, just drink and rest. If you pray, you can rest inside your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Drona. Today he hides Jayadratha behind his whole army, and the hiding place doesn't hold.
Your line: Drona: Abhimanyu, Ghatotkacha, Drona's death. Today, in the middle of whatever you're racing, take one real pause and let something rest. Day eight hundred thirty-four.

screen: `DAY 834 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: DRONA: ABHIMANYU, GHATOTKACHA, DRONA'S DEATH.`

howItsDone: The day of Jayadratha's death is told in the Drona Parva, and retellings return to the false sunset and Krishna's part in it.

match.prompt: the race against the sun — tap the pairs.
pairs: his own curse turned back on him

myth: Jayadratha came out to fight Arjuna in the open
he was hidden behind Drona's army and looked up only when the light failed.
Krishna rested and watered the horses in the middle of the battle
Arjuna stood guard while Krishna unyoked them.
the sun had truly set when Arjuna struck
the text says Krishna brought the darkness; the sun was still up.

fork.setup: you're Jayadratha. the sky goes dark and the Kauravas cheer: Arjuna's vow has failed. what do you do?
options: raise your head to look at the sky.
fork.reveal: Jayadratha looks up, Krishna says now, and Arjuna's arrow finds him before the real sunset.

original.note: the king of Sindhu who held the gap, and the target of Arjuna's vow.

trapdoor: what you thought: Arjuna simply outfought Jayadratha's guards.
what it means: he got through only because Krishna's darkness drew Jayadratha out.
what a scholar hears: the day shows the war's methods sliding: tricks on both sides, and the epic names them without hiding them.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Drona Parva (Jayadratha-vadha Parva), Drona's protection of Jayadratha, the horses watered, the darkness and Jayadratha's death

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli that Jayadratha wishes to leave and Drona promises protection, and the horses scene (Arjuna guarding while Krishna unyokes and waters them; Ganguli includes Arjuna making water and a shelter with arrows, left out here).
Confirm the darkness is attributed to Krishna's yoga power, and the Vriddhakshatra curse and the head falling into his lap at evening worship.

Editor: replaced the narrator's verdict 'the war is teaching everyone to win by any means' with two readings of Krishna's act, so the tradition is framed fairly; howItsDone no longer sizes the passage.
Original word जयद्रथ: confirm form and pronunciation.
Auditor: original pronunciation corrected to juh-yuh-DRUH-tuh (ja-ya-dra-tha syllables).
